title: AssuranceRequirement
description: The minimum authentication assurance a risk-sensitive operation demands before it may proceed (ADR-0015 §37-39 'Step-Up Authentication', §181). A caller's AuthenticationAssurance (authentication-assurance.schema.json) satisfies this requirement when (1) its acr is at least minimum_acr; (2) where the requirement names accepted_acr_values or accepted_methods, EITHER its acr is one of accepted_acr_values OR at least one of its amr entries is in accepted_methods; and (3) when set, its authenticated_at/step_up_at is no older than max_authentication_age_seconds. Both forms of evidence are issuer-authenticated. A requirement may name either form or both; naming neither means acr at or above minimum_acr suffices. phishing_resistant_required never relaxes: it states that the evidence in (2) must be of a phishing-resistant authentication.

minimum_acr.description: The lowest OIDC acr value this operation will accept.

accepted_acr_values.description: Trusted acr values whose issuer-defined meaning is itself the required evidence (for example a LoA reserved for a WebAuthn-only flow). Optional. The issuer must guarantee that no weaker flow can emit these values.

accepted_methods.description: OIDC amr values this operation will accept as method evidence. Optional: absent when acr evidence alone is sufficient.

max_authentication_age_seconds.description: Maximum age of the qualifying authentication (authenticated_at, or step_up_at when set) this operation will accept, in seconds. Absent means no freshness bound beyond acr evidence.

phishing_resistant_required.description: Whether the evidence must be of a phishing-resistant authentication (e.g. WebAuthn/passkey): a trusted phishing-resistant acr (accepted_acr_values) or an amr naming a phishing-resistant method (accepted_methods). It is never dropped to cope with an implementation limit.
